newsitem.title: GERMANY: Karstadt 5-mth sales weak, outlook upbeat.
newsitem.headline: Karstadt 5-mth sales weak, outlook upbeat.

text.p: German stores group Karstadt AG on Thursday reported weak sales for the first five months of this year at its parent Karstadt department store chain and Hertie unit, but gave an upbeat outlook for the year.

"Under the precondition that retail demand lives up to forecasts, we are optimistic of reaching our targets," chief executive Walter Deuss said about 1997 according to the text of a speech he was due to give at a new conference.
Parent sales at Karstadt rose 0.3 percent to 4.693 billion marks ($2.7 billion) from January to May but on a same store basis fell 3.4 percent.
At the group's lossmaking Hertie chain, sales fell 13 percent to 1.476 billion marks. On a same-store basis sales fell by 5.4 percent.

Mail order unit Neckermann posted five-month sales down 2.6 percent to 1.281 billion marks. The Nur Touristic travel agency chain posted sales, from November to May, up 6.3 percent to 3.061 billion marks.
The company said that despite weaker sales, its earnings from January to April were in line with plans for a substantial increase.
